name: Keystatic
title: Mica vs. Keystatic
summary: Keystatic is a polished editor for GitHub-based sites, with an optional cloud for teams. Mica works with any Git host and publishes chosen changes as one commit, but it is experimental.

chooseMica.text: Your content is on a Git host other than GitHub.
You keep large media in Git LFS. Keystatic does not support it.
An editor should publish several changes as one commit, with a summary.
You need a map field that stores the zoom, or links to reference data in a JSON or CSV file.

chooseOther.text: You need an editor that is ready for production. Mica is experimental, not ready for production.
You want a polished editor that is free to use, with saves that know about branches.
Your editors should work together in real time. Keystatic Cloud Pro has an experimental multiplayer mode.
You want Keystatic Cloud, so that editors need no server that you run.

facts.value: Yes. GitHub only. Support for GitLab is an open request. Local mode edits files on disk.
Yes. Local mode, or GitHub mode with your own GitHub App and API routes in your site. That needs a Node or SSR host. Keystatic Cloud is optional.
MIT. Keystatic Cloud is free up to 3 users. Pro costs from $10 a month plus $5 for each extra user.
Official @keystatic/astro. It needs React, Markdoc and an SSR adapter. Content comes through Content Collections or the Reader API.
GitHub App OAuth. Editors need write access on GitHub, or a fork path.
Each save is one commit to the current branch. Editors can create branches. A protected branch leads to a new branch. No batch publish.
Branch draft preview through previewUrl. The documented recipe is for Next.js only. No visual editing.
Not supported. Pull request #1514 is open.
Not documented. The relationship field links to entries by slug.
No translation of content. Issues #1553 and #1080 are open.
No roles. GitHub permissions apply. Review goes through GitHub pull requests.
